title: 36th Infantry Division 100th Anniversary (Short Version)
description: Actor Gary Sinise provides the introduction for the 36th Infantry Division, Texas Army National Guard as the division celebrates its 100th Anniversary on July 18th, 2017.  This is a shortened version of another historical video, which is also uploaded to DVIDS.  The video follows the division through the original muster at Camp Bowie, Texas, and into World War I, World War II, the Texas Army National Guard transformation through the years, the Global War on Terrorism, Defense Support to Civil Authorities and training exercises at home and abroad.  Written approval for music use has been received from the artists and recording companies.

transcript.text: ^- Congratulations to the 36th Infantry Division
^on 100 years of honorable service to our nation.
During World War I, you fought valiantly across France
and then returned to the European continent in 1943
as you stormed the Italian beaches near Salerno
during World War II.
You liberated Rome and then went on
to fight in both Germany and France.
When the homeland was attacked on September 11th, 2001,
you answered the call to fight the global war on terror
in both Iraq and Afghanistan.
You've also helped bring peace and stability
to troubled regions like the Balkans,
Central America, and the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt,
among many others.
Across Texas, you stand ready to battle floods,
wildfires, hurricanes, and whatever else may come.
As others are fleeing the storm, you're on your way in.
With both active and reserve component
soldiers in your ranks,
so many of you stand ready for any military mission,
while also maintaining civilian careers.
Since the birth of our nation,
citizen soldiers like you have answered the call
to keep us free and secure.
And we can't thank you enough.
To those Arrowhead soldiers currently deployed,
stay safe over there and come home soon.
To your families, I truly appreciate all you do
to keep the home fires burning while your soldiers are gone.
You are the unsung heroes.
On behalf of a grateful nation,
I'm proud of all the 36th has done over the last 100 years,
both at home and overseas, in spite of hell.
